A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original neural-network training experiments, optimizer comparisons, and quadratic-model simulations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original noise controls, optimizer experiments, sharpness analyses, and MNIST test-accuracy results.

M1.justification: V2 explicitly adds Dom-SGDM and Dom-Adam, projecting momentum and adaptive optimizer update vectors onto the dominant subspace (Appendix F.1). These extend the diagnostic procedures beyond the explicitly defined SGD, GD, and SAM variants in v1. The core Hessian projectors, existing update rules, and model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions study MNIST and CIFAR10 image classification, SST2 sentiment classification, and the same quadratic toy objective. V2's full-MNIST experiment changes sample coverage and adds test-accuracy evaluation within the retained classification task; it does not introduce a new dataset population or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds Noisy GD to the control comparisons, including an explicit GD-versus-Noisy-GD toy experiment (Appendix D.6). Appendix F.1 adds direct SGDM-versus-Dom-SGDM and Adam-versus-Dom-Adam comparisons; v1's momentum/Adam experiments instead report effective learning rates and training losses. The original comparison groups remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces controlled Gaussian-noise scales of 0.01, 0.05, and 0.1, a batch-size sweep from 50 to 5000, additional large-learning-rate experiments, and optimizer-projection switching protocols. Appendix H adds full-MNIST training and test-accuracy evaluation. These substantially expand experimental design; the original main-experiment settings remain documented.

E4.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the mechanism analyses through noise-scale and batch-size controls, additional Dom-GD displacement measurements, and a Noisy-GD toy experiment (Appendix D). It also adds direct momentum/Adam projection tests, effective-learning-rate trajectories, and sharpness comparisons under dominant and bulk updates (Appendices F–G). These address questions beyond the analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same mean and standard-deviation summaries over the first 1000 steps in Tables 1–3. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's Gaussian-noise variances are experimental settings, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical values, but v2 adds substantial findings: stronger alignment with more injected noise or smaller batches, failure of Dom-SGDM and Dom-Adam to reduce loss, and opposing sharpness behavior under dominant and bulk updates. Figure 45 newly shows Bulk-SGD tracking SGD's test accuracy while Dom-SGD stalls. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under changed settings.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the displacement sign in both effective-learning-rate definitions, making ordinary GD's positive rates consistent with the examples and unchanged tables. It also adds Definition 3 distinguishing gradient-flow and edge-of-stability regimes using maximum stable sharpness. The original quadratic reasoning remains, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims that dominant-only updates fail and bulk components enable learning are retained. V2 qualifies the stochastic-noise explanation to the gradient-flow regime and makes the distinct edge-of-stability self-stabilization mechanism an explicit core contribution (Sections 1.1 and 7). The added optimizer evidence largely supports claims already asserted in v1's Section 6.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops the causal interpretation by distinguishing noise-driven alignment from edge-of-stability self-stabilization and discussing their combined action in SGD. Appendix G adds hypotheses connecting dominant-component noise to sharpness reduction before reaching the minimizer manifold. Appendix H introduces a preliminary generalization interpretation while explicitly leaving broader validation open.

D1.justification: V2 documents noise distributions, sweep values, additional learning rates, and momentum parameters for the added experiments. Its new reproducibility statement says scripts and execution instructions accompany supplementary material, although their availability cannot be verified from these PDFs. The architecture descriptions, PyTorch setup, hardware, and reference implementation link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 expands the distinction between trajectory-PCA subspaces and Hessian eigenspaces and adds discussion of low-rank learning, stochastic stability, and noise-induced regularization. It adds works such as Yaras et al. (2024) and Agarwala and Pennington (2024), while removing Cosson/Jadbabaie (2023) references and leaving former Jastrzebski citations unresolved. The central positioning relative to Gur-Ari et al. remains.

P1.justification: Much of the original exposition and the sequence of Sections 1–6 remain. V2 revises the abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion, standardizes regime terminology, moves Related Work to Appendix A, and adds a reproducibility statement. It also introduces unresolved citations and several incorrect cross-references.

P2.justification: V2 adds extensive multi-panel displays for noise controls, optimizer projections, effective-rate trajectories, sharpness, and test accuracy. It also adopts conference typography and layout and relocates retained displays. Figures 2–3 shorten their displayed horizon from 40000 to 20000 steps; this alone does not establish a changed training budget.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for the central mechanism through independent noise manipulations and batch-size controls, and supplies direct projection experiments for the momentum/Adam claim asserted in v1. The clearer distinction between training regimes and corrected effective-rate definitions improve scientific precision. These gains outweigh the introduced citation and cross-reference defects, although generalization evidence remains preliminary and uncertainty reporting is unchanged.
